newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland clears Mostostal Krakow shares for trade.
newsitem.headline: Poland clears Mostostal Krakow shares for trade.

text.p: The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) has approved for public trade shares in construction firm Mostotal Krakow SA, which plans to enter the main market of the Warsaw bourse, the KPW's head said on Friday.
"Mostostal Krakow shares have been approved for public trade," Jacek Socha told a news conference on Friday after the commission cleared for trade all the firm's 9,320,000 shares.
Mostostal President Stanislaw Osieka, also present, said the firm would apply to the Warsaw Stock Exchange next week to have its shares listed.
He said the firm did not need to raise capital through a public offering, though a share issue could happen next year.
Osieka also said the firm would propose to shareholders in May next year a 1996 dividend of 30-percent of net profit.

Mostostal Krakow, which specialises in building roads and other municipal and industrial projects, expects to lift net profit to 4.2 million zlotys this year and 5.5 million zlotys next year from 2.1 million zlotys in 1995. It expects to raise consolidated profit to 8.4 million zlotys this year and 9.7 million zlotys next year from 5.7 million zlotys in 1995.
Parent sales were at 96 million zlotys last year and 67.2 million zlotys over this year's first half.

Mostostal's main shareholders are the state treasury, with 21.46 percent, food trader Cross Torg Sp zoo, with 21.14 percent, and a PBR subsidiary, investment fund Pierwszy Polski Fundusz Rozwoju PBR Sp zoo, with 10.89 percent. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
